newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania expects IBCA credit rating within weeks.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania expects IBCA credit rating within weeks.

text.p: Lithuania will announce its credit rating from European-based International Banking Credit Agency (IBCA) before the New Year or early in January, Finance ministry official told Reuters on Friday.
This will be the second credit rating for Lithuania which received a Ba2 rating from U.S. credit agency Moody's in September this year for foreign currency bonds and notes.
"Lithuania expects the IBCA rating to be higher," senior Finance Ministry official Ruta Skyriene said.
Lithuania expected to receive a rating from Standard & Poor's in the first half of 1997.
Lithuania is the first of the three Baltic countries and former Soviet Union republics to receive an international credit rating.
The new right-wing government of the Baltic state, led by Homeland Union's Gediminas Vagnorius, has pledged to speed up Lithuania's economic reforms.

The Lithuanian Parliament passed the 1997 budget in December, increasing the deficit by some 100 million to 697 million litas, compared to a budget version drawn up by the former government of ex-Communists.
Many analysts say Lithuanian reforms have lagged behind its neighbours Latvia and Estonia, in opening up the economy.
